patches.value: n is the original natural n₀, including zero; E remains a subset of BasisObjects.Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Ordinary X × ℝ uses Mathlib's maximum product metric. WithLp 2 (Rn n × ℝ) uses the L² product metric: here 2 is the extended nonnegative real exponent, not the coordinate count. EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 over Fin n. The explicit j appends the last real coordinate with Fin.snoc and unj truncates at castSucc and reads Fin.last; T009 proves this is a bijective isometry. G is exactly the set of coordinate concatenations of E and I, as an image under these explicit functions, in Euclidean Rn(n+1). E001 transports dimension from the maximum product to the L² product; no unproved metric identification is definitional. H fixes the canonical Borel measurable structure locally, avoiding any extra measurability premise on X or A. content is the exact frozen basis definition; powers are ENNReal real powers, infima/suprema and nonnegative sums remain in ℝ≥0∞ with ∞ allowed. cost retains the nonempty-member supremum; for positive exponents an empty member costs zero. RealCover explicitly includes boundedness before using real diameters, and realCost uses their nonnegative finite casts. Cover is the finite extended-diameter condition, equivalent to RealCover at positive real scales. N004 supplies finiteness before any use of NNReal representatives or toReal; standard cast order/addition compatibility does not add an assumption. No M premise ports or background-note premise ports are introduced. The pinned product metric instances require Fact (1 ≤ p): this is a proof that the Lp exponent lies in the metric range, and at p=2 it is supplied by the library, not an additional project hypothesis. The pinned Prod.dist_eq is max of the coordinate distances. Fin n indexes exactly the initial n coordinates; Fin.castSucc preserves their values in Fin(n+1), and Fin.last n is the appended coordinate. In cost and content, ^ a has real exponent a on ENNReal; in the squared-distance formulas ^ 2 is the ordinary natural square of a real distance.
